messages:
From: Eliza Hammond <eliza@mediform.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency / routing ask for DPA — small-scope clarification

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As we prepare procurement for the upcoming pilot, legal have asked for a concrete statement on routing controls and a path to execution for a UK Addendum or equivalent. Two points from their note:

1) Can Redwood commit to a region-scoped TIA for the pilot only (UK residents + EU controllers), with a limited subprocessor evidence package scoped to core inference pool?
2) If Redwood cannot do a full IDTA/UK Addendum upfront, what is the minimal set of evidence (subprocessor residency snapshot, SCC mapping, logging attestations) procurement needs to greenlight contract signature today?

We'd like to avoid a hold on the MSA signature; procurement said they can sign the main DPA if we can provide a firm execution plan and an explicit trigger that will cause Redwood to attach the UK addendum within X days of evidence delivery.

I've attached our list of questions and the redlines the procurement team expects (mediform_dpa_questions.pdf). Can you confirm what you can provide within 7 business days and whether there are specific subprocessors that will need further coordination?

Best,
Eliza Hammond
Head of Security & Privacy
Mediform

From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Hammond <eliza@mediform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency / routing ask for DPA — small-scope clarification

Hi Eliza — thanks for the note and the packet. Quick answers up front, then a couple clarifying asks so we can align on the procurement trigger.

Short answers:
- We can provide a scoped evidence bundle for a pilot (subprocessor residency snapshot, a mapping of SCCs applied to the models in use, and an ingress/egress logging sample).
- We cannot pre-sign a full UK IDTA for data we can't enumerate, but we can commit to a documented execution trigger: once Mediform signs the DPA and uploads the procurement packet (security questionnaire + PO), Redwood will produce the evidence bundle and execute the UK Addendum within 15 business days, unless a named subprocessor requires additional attestation.

Clarifying asks:
1) Can you confirm the pilot volume (approx. monthly calls / tokens) and which markets (UK-only or UK+EEA)? That affects which model variants and subprocessors we include.
2) Which signature path does procurement prefer — addendum appended at signature vs. DocuSign envelope watch and follow-on signature?

Operational note: I'll spin up an internal runbook and tag procurement/legal for the 15-day SLA. Attaching a short ops note that explains routing checks and what the evidence package will look like.

Propose a 30-minute sync on Monday to finalize the trigger wording for the MSA (I'm free 11–12 PT).

Thanks —
David
Head of Platform Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Eliza — looping in a few specifics from privacy/legal side. Thanks for outlining procurement's appetite for a conditional execution flow. A couple of commitments we can make now and items that will require further coordination: 

What we can provide within 7 business days after signature + packet: 
- Subprocessor residency snapshot (CSV) showing datacenter regions for inference nodes + edge caches used for the pilot.
- Model SCC mapping document: which standard contractual clauses we apply to each model artifact for the pilot scope.
- Sample logging extract (redacted) demonstrating ingress/egress call traces and KV cache tenancy indicators.

What might extend the timeline: 
- A named subprocessors attestation: if a subprocessors' sub-contract restricts cross-border attestation we will need them to sign a one-off attestation; that can add 7–10 business days per affected provider.

Procurement trigger language (suggested): 
- "Upon execution of the DPA and delivery of the completed security questionnaire and PO, Redwood will deliver a scoped evidence package and execute the UK Addendum within 15 business days, provided no third-party subprocessor attestation delays apply."

We can also offer a technical fallback: pin the pilot to a UK-only inference pool for the first 30 days to reduce subprocessor surface — that is an operational change with a cost delta (we'll capture it in the procurement packet).

I'll be on the call Monday; Kimberly, can you surface any subprocessors you expect to be flagged so we can pre-notify them?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
